fields.label: This Item Only
fields.description: Fill ONE of these three per row: this item, or the group below, or the brand. An item named here wins and the other two are ignored. They are deliberately not filled in for you from the item - a row that showed the item's own group would read as covering every item in that group, and clearing the item later would silently make it do exactly that.

One SKU. Exactly one of Item, Item Group and Brand is set on a row - a row naming two of them reads differently to every person who opens it, and the compiler would have to guess which one the manager meant.

fields.label: Or Every Item In This Group
fields.description: Every item in the group, read when no item is named above. Groups are a tree and this takes the children too, so a group near the root is a much wider scheme than it looks.
Every SKU in the group qualifies, expanded to base item codes by the compiler so the engine is handed a flat list and never walks a tree on a phone.

fields.label: Or Every Item Of This Brand
fields.description: Every item carrying the brand, read when neither an item nor a group is named above.

Every SKU of the brand qualifies. A brand scheme is the one most often written on a whiteboard and the one most often mis-scoped, because a brand quietly gains SKUs between the day it is typed and the day it runs.

fields.label: Case Unit
fields.description: What a case means for this row, when the slab numbers are typed in cases. A shopkeeper and a manager both say two cases; only the master knows whether that is twenty-four pieces or forty-eight.

fields.label: Conversion Factor
fields.description: Base units in one case, for this row. Left at zero the compiler resolves it from the item master, which is the normal case; it is typed only where the master is wrong and a scheme cannot wait for the master to be fixed.

fields.label: Base Unit
fields.description: The unit the slab is really counted in once the conversion has happened. Shown because a manager typing cases should be able to see what the engine will actually measure.
